attempts.label: DANDI:001767
attempts.paper_title: Dopamine and glutamate regulate striatal acetylcholine in decision-making
attempts.entry_title: Striatal dopamine and acetylcholine in decision-making (Chantranupong et al. 2023)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Chantranupong, Beron, Zimmer, Wen, Wang and Sabatini (2023) on dandiset 001767, which holds fibre photometry of dopamine, acetylcholine, glutamate and terminal calcium in the ventrolateral striatum of mice in a two-armed bandit task, with the behaviour of each session. It tests trial-outcome and history coding, the anticorrelation of dopamine and acetylcholine, the effects of TelC in cholinergic interneurons and in cortical and thalamic inputs, Drd2 deletion in cholinergic interneurons, and the behaviour of each cohort. The slice recordings, histology, head-fixed and dopamine-neuron inhibition experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Chantranupong et al. (2023) from dandiset 001767

outcomes.statement: The sessions table of the dandiset's export code (manuscript_sessions.csv in github.com/bernardosabatinilab/Chantranupong-2023-NWB, which the dandiset's metadata links) can be matched to the dandiset's files by mouse and session date, and its virus codes agree with the files' channel metadata, so its figure and genotype labels can select the paper's cohorts.
outcomes.source: Added by the author (protocol, Author, step 1.4); the files carry no figure, cohort or genotype labels.
outcomes.notes: All 379 files match a row of the export table by mouse and date (the table lists 443 sessions; 64 are not in the dataset). 1164 of 1196 channel virus codes (97.3%) equal the table's; the rest are compound codes written in one place only and one session of WT65. Each mouse has one genotype label. The TelC and control groups are formed from the table's virus codes (336, 304, 301, 353, 349), whose names in the files agree, and no mouse is in two groups. The table's cohorts have the paper's sizes for the Drd2 cohort (12, 7, 8), Fig. 2 (6) and the striatum-wide TelC and mCherry mice (5 and 5); the cortical and thalamic TelC groups have 3 and 4 mice against 5 and 5. The thalamic mCherry mice carry virus 349 (retro mCherry), the cortical control's virus; the paper does not describe the thalamic control. The table's figure labels do not follow the published numbering (EDFig10, EDFig12, EDFig16).
deviations: Link claim added by the author; the table is the dandiset's own export code, linked from the dandiset metadata, at commit f9a4ca95370e8d7451f2a29d81e184dd67a735ca.

outcomes.statement: After a block transition, mice transiently increase their probability of switching ports, which brings them to the new high-reward-probability port.
outcomes.source: Results, Adaptive switching in decision-making, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 1b,c
outcomes.quote: After successive unrewarded trials resulting from reversals of the reward probability at block transitions, the mice transiently increase their probability of switching ports between trials
outcomes.notes: On the 26 Fig. 1 mice (121 sessions, 696 transitions), mean P(switch) over mice is 0.175 in the 10 trials before a transition, 0.216 in the first 10 after it and 0.174 at block positions 20 to 30. P(high port) falls to 0.119 at the transition and recovers to 0.793 by position 10; tau_highport is 2.82 trials for the mean curve and positive in all 26 mice. P(switch) rises after the transition in 21 of 26 mice.
deviations: The n = 8 mice of Extended Data Fig. 1 are not identified in the dataset; the Fig. 1 mice are used.
Most of these sessions have a high-port probability of 0.85 or 0.9; the Methods state 95%.
tau_highport is reported as -1/k of the fit, as in the code's tau_and_error, so that a recovering curve gives a positive value.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: The three-parameter RFLR model (alpha, beta, tau) predicts the switching dynamics at block transitions and the conditional switch probabilities given the past two trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Adaptive switching in decision-making, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 1f-j
outcomes.quote: the RFLR model accurately predicts the switching dynamics at block transitions as well as the probability of switching on the current trial, which depends on the choice and reward history of previous trials
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), held-out sessions, and reading (b), all sessions, the model's conditional P(switch) is within the binomial s.e. of the mice's for 1 of 8 two-trial histories (Aa). The model overestimates AB (0.34 against 0.19 to 0.22) and underestimates aB and ab. Around transitions the correlation of model and mouse is 0.970 (a) and 0.986 (b) for P(high port) and 0.803 (a) and 0.918 (b) for P(switch). With thousands of trials per history the s.e. is 0.002 to 0.03.
deviations: The RFLR likelihood of bandit_models.py is maximised with Nelder-Mead; the SGD module the code calls is not in the repository.
Model probabilities are evaluated on the mice's own choice histories (one-step prediction); the code samples choices from them.
The held-out split is 70/30 by session per mouse, a standard choice; the paper gives none.
Fig. 1 mice in place of the 8 mice of Extended Data Fig. 1.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: After side-port entry, unrewarded trials show a lower mean DA and a larger delta-Ach than rewarded trials, in DA (13 mice) and Ach (14 mice) recordings.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA are dynamically regulated, paragraph 2; Fig. 1d,e
outcomes.quote: Reward outcome greatly alters DA and Ach transients, with unrewarded trials resulting in a robust decrease in mean DA and a consistent increase in ∆Ach (Fig. 1e )

statistics.n: 13 DA mice and 14 Ach mice, trials within each mouse

outcomes.notes: After side entry mean DA is lower in unrewarded trials in 14 of 14 mice with T1 p < 0.05 under W1, W2 and the code's window (median -0.80 z, W1), and delta-Ach higher in 12 of 16 mice under each (median +0.62 z); 2 mice (W1) and 1 (W2) differ significantly the other way. T2 p < 0.001 for both signals.
deviations: The Fig. 1 cohort has 14 DA and 16 Ach mice where the paper has 13 and 14; the paper's scripts do not list their mice, so all mice the export table labels Fig1 are kept.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: Before side-port entry, mean DA and delta-Ach do not differ significantly between rewarded and unrewarded trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA are dynamically regulated, paragraph 2; Fig. 1e
outcomes.quote: Notably, the changes are significant after ('post'), but not before ('pre') side entry
outcomes.notes: Before side entry 6 of 14 DA mice differ significantly under W1 and under the code's window, all lower in unrewarded trials (median -0.05 z), and 7 of 14 under W2, which is not fewer than half. Across mice T2 gives p = 0.0045 (W1) and 0.0062 (W2) for DA. For Ach 3 of 16 mice differ under W1 and W2 (2 under the code's window), all opposite to the post effect. The criterion names W1 and W2, and W2 fails it. The count rests on one DA mouse more than the paper's 13, which cannot be identified, so with 13 mice the W2 count could fall on either side of half.
deviations: The window readings disagree for DA (W1 6 of 14, W2 7 of 14 against a rule of fewer than half). Both are required by the criterion; the code's own Fig. 1 window (-18 to 0, which includes the side-entry sample) gives 6 of 14.
The Fig. 1 cohort has 14 DA and 16 Ach mice where the paper has 13 and 14; the paper's scripts do not list their mice, so all mice the export table labels Fig1 are kept.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: An LDA classifier separates rewarded from unrewarded trials with accuracy above 80% when trained on post-side-entry signals and around 50% (chance) when trained on pre-side-entry signals.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA are dynamically regulated, paragraph 3; Fig. 1e
outcomes.quote: the LDA classification accuracy is very high when trained on the signals post-side entry (higher than 80%), but not when trained on those pre-side entry (around 50%) (Fig. 1e )
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), mean over mice. Post-entry accuracy 0.934 (W1) and 0.935 (W2) for DA, 0.837 and 0.840 for Ach; pre-entry 0.516 and 0.518 for DA, 0.539 and 0.542 for Ach. Under reading (b), every mouse, DA post exceeds 0.80 in all 14 mice (minimum 0.818) and Ach does not (WT59 0.494, WT62 0.660). Shuffled labels give 0.49 to 0.54. The measured value is DA pre, W1, reading (a).
deviations: scikit-learn's LDA with Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage replaces MATLAB's fitcdiscr with hyperparameter optimisation (an assumption; the optimised hyperparameters are regularisation amounts); 10 balanced 70/30 splits per mouse (nModels = 10 in the paper's scripts).
The Fig. 1 cohort has 14 DA and 16 Ach mice where the paper has 13 and 14; the paper's scripts do not list their mice, so all mice the export table labels Fig1 are kept.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: DA and Ach transients do not differ between trials to the port ipsilateral and contralateral to the fibre; DA shows no significant difference and Ach differences are inconsistent in direction with poor LDA accuracy.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Results, Analysis of lateralization of DA and Ach signals; Extended Data Fig. 3d-f
outcomes.quote: Differences between these trials were not statistically different for DA (Extended Data Fig. 3e). Any significant differences for Ach were inconsistent in directionality, and the LDA classification accuracy was poor

statistics.about: DA, ipsilateral against contralateral trials, per mouse

outcomes.notes: The criterion requires that no DA mouse differ. In rewarded trials 10 of 14 DA mice differ between ipsilateral and contralateral trials with T1 p < 0.05 under W1 (7 higher ipsilateral, 3 lower) and 10 under W2; 6 and 7 in unrewarded trials. The differences are small (median 0.06 z, largest 0.19 to 0.20 z) and T2 across mice is not significant (p 0.07 to 0.32). For Ach the significant differences go both ways, and the LDA accuracy is 0.648 (rewarded) and 0.619 (unrewarded) under W1, below 0.65, but 0.691 and 0.645 under W2, so the Ach part depends on the window. The DA part fails under both.
deviations: Extended Data Fig. 3 uses 7 DA mice, which cannot be identified; the 14 Fig. 1 DA mice are used.
The fibre hemisphere is taken from each channel's metadata.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: In rewarded trials with the LED cues omitted, DA after side entry is larger and DA before side entry smaller than with cues, while Ach changes in the opposite direction.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA are dynamically regulated, paragraph 4; Fig. 1f; Extended Data Fig. 4a
outcomes.quote: the DA transient in cue-omission rewarded trials is significantly increased after side-port entry and decreased before side entry, whereas Ach transients are modulated in the opposite direction
outcomes.notes: In all 4 mice and under W1 and W2, without cues mean DA after side entry is higher (+0.38 to +0.57 z, W1), before side entry lower (-0.12 to -0.26 z), and the Ach minimum after side entry lower (-0.22 to -0.61 z) and before it higher (+0.20 to +0.44 z), each with T1 p < 0.05. Delta-Ach, shown as well, moves the same way after side entry in most mice. The files do not show the cues were omitted: the no-cue sessions have 2.3 to 4.0 centre-LED onsets per trial against 1.2 to 1.9, a side-LED onset between centre and side entry in every trial of both kinds of session, and a centre-LED onset in the 2 s before centre entry in 64 to 77% of no-cue trials (34 to 73% cued). The outcome rests on the session list of the paper's script.
deviations: The cue-omission sessions and their cued pairs are taken from the paper's aa_processStats_Fig1_DA_Ach_LED.m (WT62 to WT65, 2021-11-22 against 11-08 or 11-10); nothing in the files marks them, and their LED channel still has onsets.

Assumed that the sessions of the script's list are the cue-omission sessions. The paper's own code is the only source that names them, and the files' LED channels show cue onsets in every trial of those sessions, so the files cannot confirm it.

outcomes.statement: In trials that repeat the previous port, lose-win trials have a larger mean DA and delta-Ach after side entry than win-win trials, and win-lose trials have a deeper DA dip and a larger delta-Ach than lose-lose trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA are dynamically regulated, paragraph 5; Fig. 1g; Extended Data Fig. 4d,e
outcomes.quote: Indeed, mean DA and ∆Ach signals increase post-side entry in the 'lose–win' scenario ... Conversely, for an unrewarded trial, mean DA dips more and ∆Ach rises more if this trial was preceded by a rewarded trial ('win–lose')
outcomes.notes: Under W1 and W2, aA exceeds AA in mean DA in 14 of 14 mice and in delta-Ach in 9 of 16; Aa is below aa in mean DA in 14 of 14 and above it in delta-Ach in 10 of 16 (W1) and 9 of 16 (W2), with one mouse the other way under W2. T2 p <= 0.017 for all four.
deviations: The Fig. 1 cohort has 14 DA and 16 Ach mice where the paper has 13 and 14; the paper's scripts do not list their mice, so all mice the export table labels Fig1 are kept.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA are dynamically regulated, paragraph 5; Fig. 1h; Extended Data Fig. 4d,e
outcomes.quote: Notably, these effects of expectation on DA and Ach are absent if the mouse switches ports between trials ... the signals after side-port entry are similar
outcomes.notes: In switch trials the largest count of mice with a significant difference is 5 of 14 (DA, aB against AB, W1; 1 higher, 4 lower; median -0.17 z, T2 p = 0.015). Ach aB against AB has none; Ab against ab has at most 2 mice for either signal. AB is rare (median 16 trials per mouse, 9 for Ach).
deviations: The Fig. 1 cohort has 14 DA and 16 Ach mice where the paper has 13 and 14; the paper's scripts do not list their mice, so all mice the export table labels Fig1 are kept.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: In switch trials, DA during the move from centre to side port is larger when the previous trial was unrewarded.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA are dynamically regulated, paragraph 5; Fig. 1h
outcomes.quote: Instead, the DA signals during the transition from centre to side port are greater when the previous trial was unrewarded (Fig. 1h )
outcomes.notes: Mean DA before side entry is higher after a loss in 13 of 14 mice (W1) and 14 of 14 (W2) with T1 p < 0.05, none the other way (median +0.25 z).
deviations: The Fig. 1 cohort has 14 DA and 16 Ach mice where the paper has 13 and 14; the paper's scripts do not list their mice, so all mice the export table labels Fig1 are kept.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: DA and Ach are modulated more around port entries in unrewarded trials than around the same port entries during the ITI; after side entry DA dips more and Ach rises more in unrewarded trials, with the opposite before side entry.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Results, ITI analysis of signals; Extended Data Fig. 4b,c
outcomes.quote: DA and Ach signals are modulated to a greater extent during unrewarded trials than during the ITI ... DA signals dip more while Ach signals rise more after side port entry, and the opposite changes occur prior to side port entry
outcomes.notes: Isolated ITI side entries are few (median 6 per DA mouse and 7.5 per Ach mouse, range 1 to 53). Of the 14 DA mice 12 have more than one isolated ITI entry and can be tested. After side entry DA is lower in unrewarded trials in 7 (W1) and 8 (W2) of these 12 with T1 p < 0.05, more than half under both; before side entry higher in 5 of 12. The Ach minimum after side entry is higher in 1 mouse and lower in 1 (W1), and before it lower in 5, opposite to the stated direction. Delta-Ach, shown as a variant, gives no consistent effect either.
deviations: Port exits are taken from the occupancy channels; ITI entries closer than 15 samples to any other port entry or exit are dropped, as the Supplementary Methods state.
The Fig. 1 cohort has 14 DA and 16 Ach mice where the paper has 13 and 14; the paper's scripts do not list their mice, so all mice the export table labels Fig1 are kept.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: A base GLM of behavioural events explains about a fifth of the variance of trial-associated DA and Ach signals (test R2 0.206 for each).
outcomes.source: Results, Action-outcome history shapes DA and Ach, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 5c,d
outcomes.quote: We find that it captures substantial variance across the trial-associated data (DA GLM R 2 = 0.206; Ach GLM R 2 = 0.206)
outcomes.notes: Run under every reading. The tolerance is 0.185 to 0.227. One model per mouse (G2) gives DA 0.203 (P1) and 0.212 (P2) and Ach 0.216 and 0.227, all inside; one per session (G3) gives DA 0.211 and 0.216 (inside) and Ach 0.244 and 0.249 (above); one over all sessions (G1) gives DA 0.132 and 0.138 and Ach 0.159 and 0.167 (below). Y = 3 and Y = 10 agree to 0.002. The criterion blocks the claim when readings disagree. Question for the paper's authors (finding) on how sessions and mice were pooled.
deviations: Cohort from the export table's EDFig10 sessions (10 DA mice, dLight1.1 or rDAh, and 12 Ach mice, against 8 and 9).
Reward is coded at the side entry of rewarded trials; trial segments run from 20 samples before centre entry to 20 after side exit (the claims file's standard choice).
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: Leaving out side entry or reward raises the GLM's MSE for both DA and Ach, leaving out side exit or lick raises it for Ach, and leaving out centre entry or centre exit alone does not change it.
outcomes.source: Results, Action-outcome history shapes DA and Ach, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 5f
outcomes.quote: For both DA and Ach models, the closely timed centre entry and centre exit are redundant because loss of either alone does not affect the model fit ... DA and Ach signals are more accurately reconstructed with the addition of side entry and reward predictors, and, additionally, side exit and lick enable better reconstructions of the Ach signal
outcomes.notes: The criterion fails under every one of the 12 GLM readings, so the open readings of ed5-base-glm-r2 do not change the outcome. Leaving out reward raises the DA validation MSE beyond the full model's range under all 6 DA readings (P1 and P2 by G1 to G3; rise 0.021 to 0.030); leaving out side entry does not under any (rise 0.003 to 0.008). For Ach, leaving out side entry raises it beyond the range with P1 only, reward under 5 of 6 readings, lick under G1 and G3 with P1, side exit under none (rise 0.008 to 0.012). Leaving out centre entry or centre exit keeps the median within the full model's range in 11 of the 12 signal-reading pairs; with P2 and G3 the DA median without centre entry falls just below it (0.7631 against 0.7632). The criterion fixes Y = 10 runs; with the first 3 runs, a variant, no reading has every part hold for both signals.
deviations: The test MSE splits are shared by the base and history models of each signal (one set of 10 runs).
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: Adding side entries split by the eight action-outcome histories improves the GLM, to a test R2 of 0.213 for DA and 0.214 for Ach, with a lower MSE and no overfitting.
outcomes.source: Results, Action-outcome history shapes DA and Ach, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 5f-i
outcomes.quote: This reflects an improvement in the ability of the history GLMs to capture the variance of the trial-associated data (DA GLM R 2 = 0.213; Ach GLM R 2 = 0.214) without overfitting
outcomes.notes: Run under every reading. The history model's test MSE is below the base model's in 10 of 10 runs under every reading, on the same test trials. Its test R2 is within tolerance for DA under G2 and G3 (0.214 to 0.223) and below it under G1 (0.146, 0.150); for Ach within it under G2 with P1 (0.231), and outside it otherwise (G1 0.181 and 0.188, G2 with P2 0.240, G3 0.253 and 0.257). The readings disagree. Train and test R2 are equal under G1; the train R2 exceeds the test R2 by 0.014 to 0.032 under G2 and by 0.06 to 0.08 under G3.
deviations: Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: DA signals recorded with rDAh and dLight1.1 in opposite hemispheres of the same mice are comparable in shape, with consistently smaller amplitudes for rDAh.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA release are anticorrelated, paragraph 1; Fig. 2a; Extended Data Fig. 6d
outcomes.quote: Both sensors yield comparable signals, but with consistently reduced amplitudes for rDAh
outcomes.notes: In rewarded trials the rDAh maximum is smaller than the dLight1.1 maximum in all 3 mice under every reading, after side entry (by 0.64 to 1.03 z) and before it (by 0.21 to 0.57 z), p < 0.0001. In unrewarded trials the rDAh minimum is smaller in no mouse: after side entry it is deeper in WT63 (+0.28 z) and WT64 (+0.47 z) and does not differ in WT65; before side entry it is deeper in 2 mice (W1) and 1 (W2). Trial-averaged traces correlate at 0.79 to 0.95 (WT65 rewarded 0.788). The amplitude part holds for rewarded trials only.
deviations: The 3 mice are WT63 to WT65, the Fig. 2 mice with dLight1.1 in the right hemisphere and rDAh in the left.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: DA release is highly correlated across the two hemispheres of the same mouse.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA release are anticorrelated, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 6c
outcomes.quote: we exploited the fact that the release of DA is highly correlated across hemispheres within the same mouse
outcomes.notes: The peak cross-correlation of the two dLight1.1 hemispheres is 0.633, 0.669, 0.679 and 0.488 in WT66 to WT69, at lag 0 in each; positive and synchronous, but below the 0.7 the criterion names for 'highly'.

outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA release are anticorrelated, paragraph 2; Fig. 2d
outcomes.quote: reveal that DA and Ach responses are highly anticorrelated with a positive time lag, which indicates that increases in DA might suppress Ach with a short delay (Fig. 2d )
outcomes.notes: Over whole sessions the mean cross-correlation over the 6 mice has its minimum, r = -0.224, at +2 samples (0.108 s); the other-session and circular-shift controls stay near zero (minima -0.001). Per mouse the minimum is at 0 to 2 samples.

rDAh and Ach3.0 of the left hemisphere (redL, greenL) in each mouse.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: Trial-segregated DA and Ach signals are anticorrelated with an offset of about 100 ms in rewarded and unrewarded trials, and their noise components show a similar structure.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA release are anticorrelated, paragraph 2; Fig. 2e; Extended Data Fig. 6f
outcomes.quote: We observed that the trial-segregated DA and Ach signals are anticorrelated with a time offset of around 100 ms across rewarded and unrewarded trials ... This revealed a similar correlation structure (Fig. 2e )

outcomes.statement: The two-dimensional covariance of DA and Ach fluctuations has a negative off-diagonal at which DA changes precede Ach changes by about 100 ms at most times, and it nearly disappears when the mouse enters the side port.
outcomes.source: Results, Ach and DA release are anticorrelated, paragraph 3; Fig. 2f,g
outcomes.quote: This revealed a strong time-lagged negative covariance (Fig. 2f ), which we call the off-diagonal (Fig. 2g ), showing that, at most time points, changes in DA precede changes in Ach by approximately 100 ms ... Notably, the negative, off-diagonal covariance nearly disappears when the mouse enters the side port

Its magnitude within one sample of side entry is 0.22 (side-aligned) and 0.30 (centre-aligned) of its median in unrewarded trials and 0.54 and 1.34 in rewarded trials, so it falls below a quarter only in unrewarded, side-aligned trials.

outcomes.statement: Kernels of a GLM that predicts one neuromodulator from the other show a negative interaction at about 100 ms; photometry alone predicts weakly (R2 0.116 for DA, 0.171 for Ach), and adding the photometry kernels to the history GLMs raises R2 to 0.336 for DA and 0.388 for Ach.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Results, GLM with photometry variable; Fig. 2h; Extended Data Fig. 6h
outcomes.quote: Although the DA or Ach photometry signal alone is insufficient to robustly predict the other (Extended Data Fig. 6h) (DA GLM R2 = 0.116; Ach GLM R2 = 0.171), incorporation of these photometry kernels into history GLMs for DA and Ach improves model performance without overfitting (DA GLM R2 = 0.336; Ach GLM R2 = 0.388)
outcomes.notes: Run under every GLM reading on the 6 mice (29 sessions). Photometry only, test R2 for G1, G2, G3: DA from Ach 0.072, 0.094, 0.109 (tolerance 0.104 to 0.128); Ach from DA 0.098, 0.118, 0.136 (0.154 to 0.188, all below). History GLM with photometry: DA 0.166 to 0.270 (0.302 to 0.370, all below); Ach 0.268 to 0.366 (0.349 to 0.427, inside under G2 and G3). The criterion fails under every reading. The DA kernel that predicts Ach has its most negative coefficient at +1 sample (54 ms, Ach following DA) in every model and reading (-0.098 to -0.117); the Ach kernel that predicts DA has its minimum at -1 sample, the predicted DA preceding the predictor. Y = 3 gives the same R2 to within 0.001. The criterion's requirement that the predicted signal follow the predictor in both models is asked of a reader (questions/001767.yaml); it does not change the outcome. The measured values are G1 with P1.
deviations: The other channel's z-scored signal enters with the 41 shifts of the event predictors; the legend's kernels are from the GLM with behavioural, history and photometry variables (Fig. 2h legend).
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

outcomes.statement: DA and Ach recorded in separate hemispheres are also anticorrelated at a positive lag, with a smaller positive correlation at a negative lag.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Results, Cross correlation analysis of DA and Ach transients recorded from independent hemispheres; Extended Data Fig. 6a,b

outcomes.quote: and that depended on neuromodulator binding, because they were absent in ligand-binding-site mutants of the sensors
outcomes.notes: In WT14 the mutant Ach sensor's dF/F0 range is 0.15 of the Ach3.0 range in the other hemisphere (0.0042 against 0.0280), below a quarter; in WT15 it is 0.33 (0.0086 against 0.0257), above it. WT12 carries the mutant in both hemispheres. No dLight1.1 mutant is in the dataset, so the DA part cannot be tested; the Ach part already fails the criterion's every-mouse rule.
deviations: The wild-type reference is the Ach3.0 fibre in the other hemisphere of the same mouse.
Cohorts are selected by the figure and genotype labels of the export table manuscript_sessions.csv (link-manuscript-sessions); the paper selected them from its data folders.

findings.statement: The files carry no figure, cohort, genotype or virus-construct labels; subject metadata is a placeholder in every file (age P0D, sex U, no genotype), where the paper used male mice 6 to 8 weeks old. Cohorts can be formed only from manuscript_sessions.csv of the export repository the dandiset links.

The trials tables' times (start_time, side_in_time and the others) are not on the clock of the photometry series. They are offset from the trials' own photometry sample indices by a median of -4.6 s (range -125 to +1.2 s) and drift within one session. The sample indices land on the port onsets of the event channels in every session.
In a median of 17% of trials per session (up to 43%, above 10% in 282 sessions) the trials table's photometry_center_out_index is after photometry_side_in_index, which cannot happen in the task.

The trials tables' center_laser and side_laser columns are False in every session, while the laser channel of the seven CIN-stimulation sessions has bursts starting at side entry in about a quarter of trials.

Channels whose notes name a sensor have no raw trace in 193 channel-sessions (30 mice) and no z-scored trace in 30 (14 mice). This removes the right-hemisphere dLight1.1 of all CIN-stimulation mice, the raw traces of the thalamic mCherry mice and of several Drd2 and Fig. 5 mice, and some Ach channels.
The stored baseline_f0 series is about 0.07 times the raw trace it is described as the dF/F baseline of (median ratio over channels), so dF/F0 computed with it is wrong.

The sensor field of the channel metadata holds virus codes in S950, S952, S1142 and S1143 ('279B', '333 + 304'), and three viruses are named only by number ('unknown (virus 216)', 'unknown (virus 390)', and 222 in a compound code); 216 is the Chrimson of the CIN-stimulation cohort and 222 appears to be the TelC of S1142 and S1143, neither stated.

Nothing marks the cue-omission sessions of Fig. 1f. Their LED channels have cue onsets at the trial events, as in the cued sessions, so the files do not show that the cues were omitted. They are known only from the paper's analysis script.

The slice amperometry and cell-attached recordings, the histology, the head-fixed optogenetic sessions, the stGtACR2 DAN-inhibition sessions and the dLight1.1 ligand-binding mutant are not in the dataset. The export table lists 21 mice and 64 sessions that are not in it (for example the six Fig. 4 'Chat Dat' mice and two cortical TelC mice).

Cohorts formed from the export table differ in size from the paper's in several places (Fig. 1, 14 DA and 16 Ach mice against 13 and 14; jRCaMP1b, 9 against 6; Extended Data Fig. 3, 14 DA mice against 7), and the mice of Extended Data Fig. 1 (n = 8) cannot be identified. The table's figure labels do not follow the published numbering (EDFig10, EDFig12, EDFig16).
The high-port reward probability is 0.95 in 180 of 379 sessions and 0.8, 0.85, 0.9 or 1.0 in the others; the Methods state P(high) = 95%.

Question for the paper's authors on the GLMs (Extended Data Figs. 5, 6h and 11b,c). Were models fitted per session, per mouse, or once over all sessions, and which events were predictors? Per mouse puts both base R2 of Extended Data Fig. 5 at the reported 0.206 (DA 0.203 to 0.212, Ach 0.216 to 0.227), while one model over all sessions of a genotype puts the six R2 of Extended Data Fig. 11 at the reported values (DA 0.125 to 0.163, Ach 0.208 to 0.269) and per mouse puts them above.

Question for the paper's authors on Extended Data Fig. 11d. Is the Ach measure delta-Ach or the mean z-scored Ach? The code computes both. Delta-Ach does not separate the genotypes; the mean does (one value per mouse, p = 0.0005 before side entry, p = 0.0001 after it in rewarded trials, cKO highest).

Question for the paper's authors on the windows of the Supplementary Methods. Is the side-entry sample in the 17-sample pre or post window? It bears on one claim here (7 against 6 of 14 mice with a pre-entry DA difference). And is the bootstrap of conditional switch probabilities (Extended Data Fig. 11j) over sessions or trials? Only trials give a significant history.

The seven CIN-stimulation sessions (EDFig12) carry the laser artefact in the right fibre's red channel, labelled DIO mCherry, and not in the left fibre with the Chrimson virus (216), so the illuminated hemisphere is the control one, whose dLight1.1 trace is not stored. The laser bursts last about 1.0 s, where the Methods give 1.5 s, and the Methods' statement that the artefact is removed does not apply to the stored traces.

The VLS-TelC behaviour cohort (2020) was run with a high-port probability of 0.9 or 1.0 and blocks of about 46 trials, the striatum-wide mCherry controls (2021) with 0.95 and about 36 trials; no control group in the dataset matches the VLS-TelC task parameters.

The thalamic mCherry controls (S1351, S1389, S1393, Vglut2Cre) carry virus 349, named retro mCherry, the virus of the cortical controls, at VLS fibres in both hemispheres; the Fig. 5f legend describes mCh expression in the thalamus, and the files record no injection into the thalamus.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1: the executed notebook without conclusions, achda.py and the claims file, at commit 4655a940f1.

disagreements.reason: All 379 files match the table, virus codes agree in 97.3% of channels, each mouse has one genotype, and the Drd2 (12/7/8) and Fig. 2 (6) cohort sizes match. The striatum-wide mCherry count of 5 is circular: it counts a hand-written list of 5 mice.

DA pre under W2: 7 of 14 mice significant, which is not 'fewer than half'. W1 gives 6/14 and Ach 3/16. All significant DA mice point the same way (T2 p = 0.006). Borderline, and it depends on one extra, unidentified DA mouse.
DA fails: 4-10 of 14 mice are significant in each condition. Ach passes: significant mice split 3 vs 4 in direction, and LDA averages 0.648 and 0.619, both below 0.65.
Leaving out DA side entry fails the range rule under all 12 readings, so the readings agree on that failure. Reward (both signals) and the centre-entry/centre-exit parts hold under every reading.
In unrewarded trials, rDAh's |min| is larger than dLight's in WT63 and WT64 (p < 0.0001). WT65's rewarded traces correlate at r = 0.788, below 0.8.
Not run. The 6 rDAh+Ach mice are in the data, and the kernel-lag part of the criterion does not depend on the R2 readings.
dF/F0 reading: lower in the TelC hemisphere in 4/4 mice. z-scored delta-Ach reading: fails (S952 is higher; S1143 W1 p = 0.07; S950 W1 is higher).
Not run, although the data exist (27 mice). The kernel parts of the criterion do not depend on the R2 readings.
Cortex: every TelC mouse is below the smallest mCherry under both F0 readings (3 of the paper's 5 TelC mice). Thalamus: the mCherry mice have no raw traces (data_missing).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2: the full executed notebook with its conclusions, achda.py, the claims file and the attempt record, at commit 0bdc267707. Report in transcripts/001767/verifier-2-report.md. Text corrections asked for besides the claims below: the data_missing finding gave 23 mice for 193 channel-sessions without a raw trace (30 mice; corrected, and the count is now printed in the data check), and the Summary said that every reading named is shown and the outcomes resting on one are marked, where for fig1e-reward-outcome-not-pre and ed8g-vls-telc-ach-suppressed the claims file did not leave the reading open (rewritten).

disagreements.reason: The criterion judges both W1 and W2, and the claims-file checks say claims need both window readings; W2 gives 7 of 14 DA mice, which is not fewer than half, so choosing a window is not left open to the author. The assumption's basis is weak: the claims-file header gives the Fig. 1 scripts a pre window of -18 to 0, which includes the side-entry sample, and the startDrop = -1 scripts the record cites are for other figures. The result is borderline and depends on one extra DA mouse that cannot be identified.

Same as round 1. In unrewarded trials rDAh is significantly larger than dLight1.1 in 2 of 3 mice, against 'consistently smaller'. The correlation of WT65's rewarded traces is 0.788, below 0.8. Only the rewarded half of the amplitude part holds, and the criterion fails as a whole under every reading.

The criterion says 'Reproduced when, under each reading, Ach is lower ... in every one of the 4 mice'. Reading (a) fails: S952 is significantly higher under W1 and W2, S950 is not lower under W1, and S1143 has p = 0.073 under W1. The argument that z-scoring hides an amplitude loss questions the claims file; it does not let the author pick one reading.

The criterion requires every part under every reading, and no part holds: the R2 part holds only under one model per genotype (G1); the Ach-kernel part holds only under the author's mean-over-shifts reading and fails shift by shift under every reading; the DA 'comparable' part fails under every reading. Y = 3 is not run for ed11.

entries.name: 001767-chantranupong-2023
entries.title: Striatal dopamine and acetylcholine in decision-making (Chantranupong et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Chantranupong, Beron, Zimmer, Wen, Wang and Sabatini (2023) on dandiset 001767, which holds fibre photometry of dopamine, acetylcholine, glutamate and terminal calcium in the ventrolateral striatum of mice in a two-armed bandit task, with the behaviour of each session. It tests trial-outcome and history coding, the anticorrelation of dopamine and acetylcholine, the effects of TelC in cholinergic interneurons and in cortical and thalamic inputs, Drd2 deletion in cholinergic interneurons, and the behaviour of each cohort. The slice recordings, histology, head-fixed and dopamine-neuron inhibition experiments are not in the dandiset.
